topic: The finesse: lead towards the A-Q
why: South opens 1♣ and rebids 2NT to show 18-19 points; North, with 9, raises to 3NT.
West leads the ♥Q. Count your tricks: the ♠A, the ♥A-K, four diamonds and the ♣A make eight. The ninth can come from dummy's ♠Q, but only if West has the king and you lead towards it.

Win the ♥A and lead a low spade from your hand towards dummy's A-Q. West plays low, so play the queen: it wins, because West's king has to play before dummy. Now cash the ♠A and run the diamonds: two spades, two hearts, four diamonds and the ♣A make nine tricks.
Cash the ♠A and lead the queen, hoping the king falls, and West wins the king: one down. Leading the queen from dummy is worse: West covers it with the king.
title: The finesse

hints.1: Count your top tricks. Which card in dummy could become the ninth trick, and who would need to hold the card that beats it?
hints.2: You hope West has the ♠K. Which hand should you lead from, so that West has to play before dummy?
hints.default: Lead from your hand towards dummy's ♠A-Q. If West plays low, try the queen.

traps.msg: If you take the ace, the ♠K can still beat your queen later. Play the queen now: if West has the king, it wins.

page.count: Eight top tricks; the ninth must come from dummy's ♠Q.
page.clue: West's ♥Q lead is the top of a sequence. Nothing tells you where the ♠K is, so give yourself the chance that West has it.
page.danger: Lead the queen, or cash the ace first, and the ♠K takes your queen.
page.plan: Lead low from your hand towards the ♠A-Q, and play the queen when West plays low.

questions.hint: If West has the king, which card can win?

questions.explain: It is a 50% chance, and here it is your only chance of a ninth trick.

replay: West leads the ♥Q; win the ace.
Lead towards dummy; West plays low, so play the queen.
The finesse worked; now cash the ♠A.
Now the defence take the rest.
West's king takes the last trick: 3NT made.
